summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and gastrostomy dependence was admitted with lethargy and tachypnea after a recent aspiration event at his skilled nursing facility. He presented with sepsis and hypoxemic respiratory failure, initially treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics. Respiratory cultures grew Serratia marcescens, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Providencia rettgeri, prompting a switch to meropenem. A concurrent VRE urinary tract infection was treated with linezolid. He also had recurrent C. difficile, managed with oral vancomycin, and hypernatremia corrected with free water flushes. Delirium developed in the ICU and was managed with a short course of Seroquel. His mental status and respiratory function improved, allowing weaning from ventilation and transfer to the floor. He was discharged to extended care on a full course of IV antibiotics, continuation of C. diff treatment, and instructions to restart citalopram one week after completing linezolid.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
